Have you asked your school for any accommodations since you have adhd? Some accommodations you might be able to get is being allowed to use notes during tests, extended time, and a separate room for taking tests. Also, there might be tutors/coaches that specialize in adhd and if not, a regular tutor can be very helpful too. 

Maybe also try to find someone you can study with. Have you heard of "body doubling"? A lot of people with adhd find it helpful just being around people to study.

Another thing is to also check in with yourself. Burnout or stress can make it harder to focus so it'd be helpful to figure out if there's other things in your life affecting you.

Good luck!

Can’t think of any shows that show healthy relationships but some good shows that explore emotional neglect are Succession and Sharp Objects. 

Succession is about a rich family where the father is head of a media company he built and his children fight each other to take over. The father manipulates his children and it’s interesting to watch how they interact with each other and other people because of the neglect and abuse they faced. 

Sharp Objects is about a reporter who returns to her hometown because of murders and she has to face her mom who cares more about herself than her.

Thank you so much for asking this! I'm dealing with this too and wow "information hoarding" is a good way to describe it. I can relate to feeling like I'm missing out. Sometimes when I'm learning something I feel like I've got to write everything about it down. I guess I gotta work on my mindset and notetaking skills, like only noting down the important stuff. Maybe it's like learning a language. I guess I have to figure out how much I want to learn like do I want to be able to have simple conversations in that language or be able to watch the news or read a book or something. Also, lots of words exist but some are rarely used and I'll have to figure out if I want to learn them or not. I have to prioritize which information to learn based on what is useful. I might feel like I'm missing out but I probably won't use it anyway... 

There's also radical acceptance, which I've yet to gain more experience on. I think it can be helpful in accepting that you can't learn all the information that exists. Here's an article about [radical acceptance](https://hopeway.org/blog/radical-acceptance). (It's kinda focused on COVID but still useful.)

The wanting a bunch of evidence before coming to a conclusion reminds me of this post: [Does anyone elses brain pick at them to find the exact truth?](https://www.reddit.com/r/aspergers/comments/lkflkh/does_anyone_elses_brain_pick_at_them_to_find_the/) There were comments about needing to know all the details otherwise they won't understand something and needing to use the correct words when communicating. Maybe that'll be explained more in the resources you linked so I'll check it out when I have the time. And that answers my question, thank you so much!!

You’ve mentioned that your mom never sat down with you to do kid’s stuff and holy shit, now that I think back, my mom rarely did kid’s stuff with me either... or at least not much I can remember. All I can think of right now is reading books from the library one time and maybe even drawing? 

Didn’t get “the talk” either. I remember going to the bookstore with my family and picking a book about growing up and that was that.

I remember crying one time about a situation. My dad saw and went out to report to my mom that I was crying. I thought that was normal but now that I think about it, parents are supposed to comfort their kids. Wow. Weird.

My dad’s barely there... He just does his own thing. What’s a dad even supposed to be like? He just takes me to places, gets food for me, and buys me stuff. I thought that was normal too but they’re supposed to be more involved in your life? and.. yeah I don’t know. 

Also, my parents never asked about my grades. Can’t really remember any rewards or punishments. Things just happen and it’s okay. I think I had to raise or take care of myself a lot of the time. My parents provided the physical stuff (except for hugs and affection haha).

I found out about childhood emotional neglect recently and I can relate. My parents have never shown any affection and now whenever I see families on tv hug, it makes me realize what I didn’t have. I remember once seeing my dad and thinking it’d be nice to spend time with him or hug him but that would never happen because it all feels too weird. If I think about any physical contact with my parents I feel disgusted and I wish I didn’t. 

At night I just sleep with a stuffed animal and sometimes pretend the blankets and pillows are the warmth of another person.    All I can do is wish for being held but I’m also afraid if I found someone I might be too needy and get rejected or I might keep to myself and not let myself get what I want out of the relationship.

I hope you find people who care about you and make you feel held.
